r9-a01-get-bound.reachability: public X_get on X_default() (vectors) or on a list built with X_append (progressive lists); X_get -> X_get_n -> X_get_in (patched test). Contract (docs/API_CONTRACTS.md, X_get): None for i >= length.
r9-a01-get-bound.counterexample: X_get(X_default(), N) for Vector[_, N] (or X_get(l, len(l)) for a progressive list): unmutated None, mutant Some(the bytes past the last element)

r9-a02-set-bound.reachability: public X_set on X_default(); X_set -> X_set_n -> X_put_at (patched test).
r9-a02-set-bound.counterexample: X_set(X_default(), N, x): unmutated ok = 0 and the object unchanged, mutant ok = 1 and bytes written past the last element (a later X_serialize refuses or hashes them)

r9-a03-set-no-index-check.reachability: public X_set; X_set -> X_set_n -> X_put_at (the index test removed).
r9-a03-set-no-index-check.counterexample: X_set(X_default(), N, x) answers ok = 1 (and any index writes through the word mask of the storage)

r9-a04-set-value-range.reachability: public X_set of a uint8 / uint16 vector; X_set -> X_set_n (patched range test) -> O.words_write (masks to the width).
r9-a04-set-value-range.counterexample: X_set(X_default(), 0, 2^k) answers ok = 1 and stores 0 (the value is truncated)

r9-a05-len-unit.reachability: public X_len, and X_get / X_set through it.
r9-a05-len-unit.counterexample: X_len(X_default()) answers the byte count; X_get(v, N) answers Some

r9-a06-get-position.reachability: public X_get -> X_get_in -> X_at (patched stride / width).
r9-a06-get-position.counterexample: X_get(X_set(X_default(), 1, x), 1) answers a value other than x

r9-a07-set-position.counterexample: X_set(X_default(), 1, x) then X_get(_, 1) / X_serialize differ from the spec value with element 1 = x

r9-a08-bool-read.reachability: public X_get of a boolean vector / progressive list -> X_at -> X_bool_at (patched).
r9-a08-bool-read.counterexample: X_get(X_default(), 0) answers Some(True) for a False element

r9-a09-append-slot.counterexample: three appends 7, 8, 9: X_get(l, 2) / X_serialize differ from [7, 8, 9]

r9-b03-bitvec-write.counterexample: bvN_set(bvN_set(bvN_default(), 2, 171), 1, 171): byte 2 is cleared by the second write

r9-d01-getter-neighbour.reachability: public field getter <Name>_get_<f> (or the group getter it calls) on an object built with public setters.

r9-d01-getter-neighbour.verdict_if_probe_silent: critical (argued: the getter returns another field for every object whose two fields differ)

r9-d02-setter-neighbour.counterexample: <Name>_set_<f>(o, v) changes field g instead of f

r9-d03-swap-noop.reachability: public <Name>_swap_<f> (the getter / setter of a non-copyable field).
r9-d03-swap-noop.counterexample: <Name>_swap_<f>(o, w) answers (o unchanged, w) instead of (o with f = w, old f): the old field is lost to the caller and the new one is not stored

r9-d05-top-setter-route.reachability: public <Name>_set_<f> of a grouped container -> <Name>_g<k>_set_<g> (patched routing).

r9-e01-group-validity.reachability: public <Name>_valid (and the containers whose validity calls it) -> <Name>_valid_f -> <Name>_g<k>_valid (patched conjunct). The checked serializer of these names does NOT call _valid (it uses the writers' poison flags), so the fault changes X_valid only.
r9-e01-group-validity.counterexample: an object whose named field is invalid: X_valid answers 1 while X_serialize refuses (contract: X_serialize ok = False exactly for objects that are not X_valid)
